correctness.rationale: For the ordered-pair graph, the verifier enumerates exactly 1949 and 28820 nonempty independent sets with respective face vectors (20,150,520,815,444) and (30,360,2200,7170,11700,7360). Its pivot-toggle matching has respectively 959 and 13922 pairs. Full directed Hasse-poset topological sorts verify 7340 and 138660 arrows and leave critical cells (1,6,24) in dimensions (0,3,4), respectively (1,7,968) in dimensions (0,4,5). Exact signed gradient-path elimination calculates cellular boundary matrices 6x24 and 7x968; each has a unit coefficient and all 2x2 minors zero, hence rank one and sole Smith invariant one. Since all low nonzero dimensions are >=3 and no intermediate CW cells exist, Hurewicz identifies attaching maps with degree vectors; unimodular cancellation proves wedge multiplicities (5,23) and (6,967). Independently enumerated partial functions yield identical mod-2, mod-3, and mod-5 homology. Complete finite proof only for n=5,6.

originality.rationale: Direct arXiv primary full-text comparisons: Engström (math/0512420v1) analyzes connectivity for claw-free graphs; Barmak (1007.0418v1) gives general reductions and a triangle-free suspension theorem inapplicable to clique-containing truncated-simplex graphs; Goyal–Shukla–Singh (1905.06926v1) treats different families (categorical products and generalized Mycielski graphs). Searches for exact truncated-four/five-simplex independence-complex decompositions, partial-function and directed-arc aliases, and exact sphere multiplicities found no covering statement. Indexed neighboring results describe other graph families or Rips complexes, not either claimed graph independence complex. Actual current and preceding research-ledger recoverable claims have no matching statement. Residual risk is an equivalent unindexed or unpublished computation; absence of a hit is not proof of priority. The line-graph identity T_m=L(sd K_m), where sd K_m subdivides every edge once, was explicitly checked; matching-complex/subdivided-complete-graph aliases were also queried and no indexed covering result found. Barmak §5 gives connectivity bounds for matching complexes, not these two homotopy equivalences.
residual_risks: A full-text-equivalent calculation might exist in literature not returned by the searches; absence from an index cannot prove priority.

value.rationale: The two first higher-dimensional truncated-simplex graphs (20 vertices, 40 edges; and 30 vertices, 75 edges) are canonical geometric objects, with independence complexes naturally encoding partial functions without fixed points or mutual reversals. The exact integral homotopy types have nonzero spheres in two adjacent degrees and large, strongly differing upper multiplicities 23 and 967. Existing general connectivity results do not determine these homotopy invariants; the unit attaching map resolves integral information not implied by ranks alone. The paired, natural adjacent-dimensional calculation supplies reproducible structural benchmarks for studying truncated-simplex independence complexes, while making no infinite-family claim.
